subject.title: Feature: Built-in pace-aware rate limiting for autonomous agents

question: Should OpenClaw add core pace-aware provider usage controls for autonomous agents, and should the first phase be observability-only or include opt-in enforcement?
rationale: The issue would add provider-specific usage semantics, persisted pace state, new config/defaults, status/session_status output, and subagent throttling behavior, while discussion notes that naive utilization tiers can misroute or over-throttle work.

options.title: Observability first
options.body: Capture and expose provider pace context in status/session surfaces without blocking agent work until maintainers validate the data model and UX.

options.title: Opt-in enforcement
options.body: Add disabled-by-default pace thresholds for subagents with explicit config, tests, and recovery behavior in the same design pass.

options.title: Plugin or API seam
options.body: Keep core lean by adding only generic provider/agent hooks and letting a plugin own provider-specific pace policy.

recommendation.title: Observability first
recommendation.body: Capture and expose provider pace context in status/session surfaces without blocking agent work until maintainers validate the data model and UX.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent and historical signal across provider usage, status, and config-adjacent code paths involved in the decision.
